Header: Cercospora coffeicola (Brown Eye Spot, Berry Blotch in English)

Prevention: Brown-eye spot is a fungal disease that spreads by wind and rain splash, favoured by humid-warm conditions.
In the nursery, ensure plants are adequately spaced and provide some shading (50%).
Provide good aeration by opening the soil lightly with a garden fork in seedling stage while still in nursery.
Buy clean coffee seedlings from a certified nursery.
Ensure that nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium are applied to the soil.
Phosphorus deficiency increase the susceptibility of the plants.
Prune the coffee bushes to allow good aeration.
Select a spacing at 10ft x 10ft for robusta coffee.
Prune coffee adequately and cultivate with some shade to avoid any stress such as overbearing or sun-scorch that can make the berries particularly susceptible.
Monitoring: In the nursery the disease can cause leaf fall and stem dieback in severe cases.
Be vigilant during warm humid conditions because spores need water to germinate.
Look for reddish brown spots (5-15mm) with ash grey centres on the upper leaf surface.
Spots may have yellow halo with a small olive-green patch within the grey centre.
Consider action to prevent further spread to uninfected trees when yellow or red appear on berries on 10-15% of trees.
Monitor seedlings and young nursery plants and apply fungicide when the disease becomes apparent >50% of plants.
Look for reddish dark brown patchy lesions on the berries (berry blotch) like those of coffee berry disease but with a yellow to red halo and not sunken.
Small raised red spots (red blister) appear on green or ripening berries.
But action is too later then.
Infected and damaged coffee trees cannot be cured.
Direct Control: Remove infected twigs branches and berries and burn away from the field because they are a source of infection.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage, timing of application, pre-harvest interval, max number of sprays, restricted re-entry interval.
Do not empty into drains and water sources.

There is no synthetic fungicide that can cure an infected tree.
There are only protective contact fungicides that may prevent uninfected trees to become infected.
For foliar sprays, thorough coverage of leaves is required.
